The assembler was opening a shrink wrapped bundle of cartons on the packing bench. The task was underway because the bundle was needed to keep the packing line running through the shift. Stage of the task: in process - normal running work. Method in effect: No written procedure exists for this task. No written procedure exists for this task. Equipment involved: Utility knife with a retractable blade, issued from the tool crib. Equipment state at the time: at rest or stopped. Equipment condition: The blade had not been changed for several weeks and was noted as dull by the packer. Object handled weighed approximately 12 pounds for the bundle. Object size and shape: about 24 by 16 by 10 inches, wrapped tight with no hand holds. The object was held as follows: the bundle was steadied with the left hand while the assembler drew the knife toward the body with the right hand. PPE in use: Safety glasses and cut level A2 gloves. This differed from the PPE specified for the task. Immediately before the event: standing at the packing bench with the bundle at waist height, left hand flat on the top of the bundle and the right hand holding the knife about 6 inches away. At the moment of the event: the blade cut through the wrap sooner than expected, the knife continued travelling toward the body, and it contacted the left index finger which was resting on the wrap. Immediately after the event: the knife was set down on the bench, the cut was covered with the right hand, and the team lead was called over from the next station. The assembler struck against a stationary object. Mechanism: The knife blade was moving toward the body and the left index finger was stationary on the bundle. Direction and distance of travel: toward the body over a travel of about 6 inches. Mass or speed of the object: light hand force, but the blade was drawn rather than pushed. Point of contact and direction of force: across the palm side of the left index finger at the middle joint, with the blade travelling toward the thumb side. Difference from a normal run of this task: The dull blade needed more force than usual, which is why the cut released suddenly. Conditions at the point of injury: time or production pressure. Detail: The packing line was running behind and cartons were being opened faster than normal. Timing: About 5 hours into an 8 hour shift and roughly 2 minutes into this task. The assembler had performed this task before. A known hazard, prior near miss, open action or risk assessment covers this task. Detail: Cutting toward the body has been raised at two toolbox talks and safety knives were requested for the packing bench about three months ago. A guard, interlock, barrier or control was bypassed, missing, defeated or ineffective. Detail: A self retracting safety knife is the specified control for this bench but none were available in the tool crib. Stop-work opportunity: The employee could have waited for a safety knife to be issued, but that would have stopped the packing line for an unknown period. First aid at the scene: The wound was rinsed at the sink and a sterile dressing with pressure was applied in the first aid room. This was given by a trained first aid responder. Notification: The team lead was told immediately and EHS was notified within about ten minutes. Scene and equipment: The station was left as it was and the area supervisor attended before work resumed. Work at the location stopped. The assembler was sent to an offsite occupational clinic for evaluation.
